Freshly painted 'School - Keep Clear' markings have appeared outside an empty field in a Huntingdonshire village. The markings have appeared in Sawtry outside the site of Saltbrook Primary Academy, a long-promised two-form-entry school. But the school has not yet received planning permission or been built. Cllr Simon Bywater, county councillor for Sawtry and Stilton, said: "There’s just one rather significant problem. School Keep Clear signs have appeared on a road in Sawtry outside an empty field where a primary school has been planned for years, but is yet to be built. "The school they are apparently there for hasn’t even got planning permission yet, let alone been built. "This is the same school that residents have been promised for years, and which formed part of the justification for the closure of Gidding School a number of years ago. "Yet here we are. "We’ve got the school road markings before we’ve got the school." School Keep Clear signs have appeared on a road in Sawtry outside an empty field where a primary school has been planned for years, but is yet to be built. Plans for the school date back to 2021, when outline permission was granted for a wider development in northern Sawtry. The plans included land reserved for a primary school. Cambridgeshire County Council has since submitted detailed plans for Saltbrook Primary Academy, to be built in two phases. The first phase includes a one-form-entry school for 210 pupils, an early-years facility and infrastructure for future expansion. It will eventually expand to two-form entry, with room for up to 420 pupils. Read more Cambs man who filmed himself sexually assaulting sleeping woman jailed Cambridgeshire ‘school streets’ could be enforced with cameras Woman sexually assaulted in Hunts village as police ramp up patrols The fascinating history of St Ives island's basket makers Vape related blazes cost Cambs fire service more than £850 in just three years Cllr Bywater raised the issue in a letter to senior county council officers and the chair of the children and young people's committee. He described the situation as "poorly coordinated" and said it had caused "considerable and understandable frustration among local residents." He also questioned the decision to paint a bus stop marking at the site when no bus service currently operates there. He said: "Given how long residents have waited for this much-promised school, the premature installation of these markings is rubbing salt into the wound. "It creates the impression that resources and attention are being directed towards road markings when they are urgently needed elsewhere, before the fundamental issues surrounding the school’s approval and delivery have been resolved." He demanded an explanation of why the markings were installed, who authorised the work and whether the bus stop would ever become operational. Meridian Trust will run the new school, which is intended to serve children from Sawtry's new housing developments. The school is expected to open initially to Reception applications only before expanding as its first intake moves through the years. The council says construction will be timed using pupil forecasts and ongoing monitoring of numbers in the area. The first phase is expected to be completed before the school is needed. The council, Department for Education and Meridian Trust will keep the opening date under review to meet community needs without undermining Sawtry's existing schools. He said: "For local residents who have waited patiently for this much-promised new school, I can completely understand why the irony of these markings has not gone unnoticed. "Perhaps the county council administration could apply the same urgency to actually delivering the school as it has to painting the road outside it." He called on the county council to issue a formal statement addressing residents' concerns. Mr Bywater also said MP Ben Obese-Jecty had been kept informed and had asked to be briefed as the situation developed. A Cambridgeshire County Council spokesperson said: “These school road markings have been installed prematurely in error by contractors working on behalf of the Glatton Road housing developer. “As a school is not yet operational at this location, we have asked the developer to remove these school markings as a priority and at their own expense.” The early years facility is planned to provide 52 places, subject to demand, while the school design includes roof-mounted solar panels, natural ventilation and reduced reliance on artificial lighting.
